title: Nullable reference types are enabled
rationale: The compiler tracks null; this is C#'s answer to Option.

title: The latest analyzers run at full strength
rationale: AnalysisLevel latest-all enables every built-in analyzer.

title: Code style is enforced in the build
rationale: EnforceCodeStyleInBuild makes .editorconfig style rules fail builds.

title: Package versions are managed centrally
rationale: Directory.Packages.props keeps one version per package across projects.
hint: Copy templates/csharp/Directory.Packages.props and move every PackageReference Version into it.

title: Microsoft packages are preferred over third-party ones
rationale: The BCL and Microsoft.Extensions cover most needs with long-term support.

title: Unsafe code is off
rationale: Without unsafe blocks the runtime guarantees memory safety, which is the closest C# gets to Rust. A Win32 call that cannot avoid pointers lives in one reviewed adapter project instead.
hint: Set AllowUnsafeBlocks to false in Directory.Build.props. LibraryImport needs unsafe; use classic DllImport without pointers in one adapter.

title: Integer overflow throws
rationale: Unchecked arithmetic wraps silently, so a wrong counter, size or address looks valid. A thrown OverflowException is a visible bug.
hint: Set CheckForOverflowUnderflow to true; wrap deliberate wrapping (hashes, checksums) in an unchecked block with a comment.

title: MSBuild and NuGet warnings are errors too
rationale: TreatWarningsAsErrors covers the compiler and analyzers only. MSBuild and NuGet warnings (vulnerable package, missing lock file) stay green without this switch.
hint: Set MSBuildTreatWarningsAsErrors to true next to TreatWarningsAsErrors.

title: Banned APIs are enforced by an analyzer
rationale: A rule in a document is forgotten; a build error is not. BannedApiAnalyzers fails the build on a listed API and names the allowed alternative.
hint: Copy templates/csharp/BannedSymbols.txt and the PackageReference plus AdditionalFiles items of templates/csharp/Directory.Build.props.

title: Banned APIs cover wall-clock time and blocking waits
rationale: DateTime.Now makes time-dependent code untestable (inject TimeProvider). Task.Wait and Task.Result block the caller and deadlock a UI thread. These two classes cause most flaky tests and frozen windows.
hint: Add the time and task entries of templates/csharp/BannedSymbols.txt.

title: Package restore is reproducible
rationale: Lock files pin the whole dependency graph, transitive packages included, so a build next year restores what was reviewed today and a changed graph shows up in the diff.
hint: Set RestorePackagesWithLockFile to true, commit every packages.lock.json and restore with --locked-mode in CI.

title: Known vulnerable packages fail the build
rationale: NuGetAudit reports advisories as warnings; with warnings as errors a vulnerable package stops the build. Mode all includes transitive packages, where most advisories hide.
hint: Set NuGetAudit to true and NuGetAuditMode to all.

title: The .NET SDK version is pinned
rationale: Analyzer sets and compiler behaviour change between SDK versions. global.json makes every developer PC and the pipeline build with the same one.
hint: Add global.json with sdk.version and rollForward latestFeature.

title: Tests run on Microsoft.Testing.Platform
rationale: It is the runner Microsoft ships for MSTest 4 and .NET 10: no VSTest host process, faster startup, and the same behaviour with dotnet test and Visual Studio.

title: Warnings are never silenced with a blanket NoWarn
rationale: A NoWarn in the build props hides a diagnostic everywhere and without a reason. A suppression in .editorconfig or [SuppressMessage(Justification)] is local and explains itself.
hint: Remove NoWarn; fix the code or suppress the single diagnostic in .editorconfig with a comment.

title: C# style rules are configured
rationale: EnforceCodeStyleInBuild (CSH-004) only enforces what .editorconfig asks for. Without a C# section there is nothing to enforce and the severities are the IDE defaults.
hint: Copy the [*.cs] section of templates/csharp/.editorconfig and raise the severities you want enforced to warning.

title: Formatting is verified in the gate
rationale: dotnet format --verify-no-changes turns the style rules into a pass/fail gate that works the same locally and in CI, so no PR carries formatting noise.
hint: Run dotnet format <solution> --verify-no-changes before every commit and in the pipeline; name it in CLAUDE.md.
